title: Strict complete monotonicity conjecture for $F_3$
statement: Let $F_3$ be the function defined in Theorem 3 of the source paper. A function is **strictly completely monotonic** on an interval if all of its derivatives have alternating signs there, namely $(-1)^kF_3^{(k)}(x)>0$ for every integer $k\geq 0$ and every $x$ in the interval. **Strict complete monotonicity conjecture.** The function $F_3$ is strictly completely monotonic on $(0,1/2]$. If true, this would yield sharp lower and upper bounds for $R(x)$ expressed in terms of $B(x)/[1+x(1-x)]$ and polynomials.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.07712

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2018).
source_name: Song-Liang Qiu, Xiao-Yan Ma and Ti-Ren Huang, “Sharp Approximations for the Ramanujan Constant”, arXiv:1804.07712 (2018).
